name: Saku PWA – App Mode & Mobile Bottom Bar
author: yatnozigana

sections.description:
Saku PWA turns any WordPress site into a Progressive Web App and gives mobile visitors the navigation they already know from native apps, in one small plugin.

Installable app

  • Web app manifest generated from your settings, with name, colours, start page and orientation.
  • Uses your Site Icon automatically, or an icon you upload (192 and 512 px sizes are created for you).
  • Service worker with network-first pages and cached styles, scripts, images and fonts.
  • Offline fallback page you can edit.
  • App shortcuts (long-press the app icon on Android) built from your bottom bar items.

Mobile bottom bar

  • Up to 5 items with a built-in line icon set, no icon font to load.
  • Show it to all mobile visitors, or only when the site is opened as an installed app.
  • Three styles (glass, solid, dark), optional raised centre button and labels.
  • The current page is highlighted automatically.
  • Common “back to top” and chat buttons are lifted above the bar.

App-like touches

  • “Install app” banner: one tap on Android, a clear Share › Add to Home Screen hint on iPhone. Closed banners stay hidden for 7 days.
  • Thin loading bar while the next page opens.
  • Smooth page transitions in standalone mode.
  • Offline / back online notice.

Built to be light and safe

  • No external CDN, fonts or tracking. Everything is served from your own site.
  • Admin, login, REST API, previews, cart, checkout and account pages are never cached.
  • Pages rendered for logged-in users are never cached.
  • Saving the settings refreshes the cache on returning visitors’ devices.
  • Removal mode cleanly unregisters the service worker before you uninstall.

Settings screen with a live phone preview

Configure everything under Settings › Saku PWA and watch a phone preview update as you type.

Developers

  • sakupwa_manifest filter: change the manifest array.
  • sakupwa_nav_items filter: change the bottom bar items.
  • sakupwa_sw_skip_patterns filter: add paths the service worker must never cache.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the saku-pwa folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings › Saku PWA, set your app name, colours and bottom bar items, then click Save settings.
  4. Clear your page cache if you use a caching plugin.

Your site must be served over HTTPS for browsers to allow installation.
sections.faq:
Does it work with my theme?

The bottom bar is a fixed element added in the footer, so it works with most themes. It is shown on screens up to 768 px wide and adds bottom padding so your content is not covered.

Can I use it together with another PWA plugin?

No. Two service workers on the same site conflict. Deactivate other PWA plugins first; Saku PWA shows a warning if it finds one.

Which icon is used for the app?

In this order: the icon you upload in Saku PWA, your WordPress Site Icon, then the built-in icon.

Will visitors see old content?

Pages are fetched from the network first and only served from the cache when the visitor is offline. Every time you save the settings, the cache version changes and returning visitors receive fresh files.

How do I remove the app completely?

Turn on Removal mode under Settings › Saku PWA › Advanced, keep it on for a few days so returning visitors’ devices unregister the service worker, then deactivate and delete the plugin. Deleting the plugin removes its settings and generated icons.

Is any data sent to external services?

No. The plugin does not contact any external service and does not collect personal data. The “install banner closed” choice is stored in the visitor’s own browser (localStorage) only.
